content.text:
Memory: Store and recall persistent memory across sessions using a local knowledge graph.
By MCP reference servers. AI & Machine Learning. Verified by mcp.tc: official server from MCP reference servers.
Listing page: https://mcp.tc/i/memory
Install command: npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory
Access: Runs on your computer, started by your client.
Memory is a reference MCP server that gives an assistant a knowledge-graph-based persistent memory. Information is kept between conversations so the assistant can recall it later. It runs locally over stdio with npx (npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory) and is configured in an MCP client such as Claude Desktop. No API key is listed. The maintainers describe the repository's servers as reference implementations for learning, not production-ready solutions.
Setup (call get_server with client=<id> for the full steps):
- Claude Code (claude-code): `claude mcp add --transport stdio memory -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory`
- Claude Desktop (claude-desktop): see client=claude-desktop
- Cursor (cursor): Add to Cursor: https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=memory&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoibnB4IiwiYXJncyI6WyIteSIsIkBtb2RlbGNvbnRleHRwcm90b2NvbC9zZXJ2ZXItbWVtb3J5Il19
- VS Code (vscode): `code --add-mcp '{"name":"memory","type":"stdio","command":"npx","args":["-y","@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"]}'`
- Devin Desktop (devin): see client=devin
- Codex (codex): `codex mcp add memory -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory`
- Gemini CLI (gemini): `gemini mcp add memory npx -- -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory`
- Any client (json): see client=json

setup.label: Claude Code
steps: Run this in a terminal, in your project folder:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport stdio memory -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory
```
Start Claude Code and type `/mcp`. **memory** should show as connected.

setup.note: Add `--scope user` to make it available in every project.
